about: The quick checks before a push (tools/quick.mjs; CLAUDE.md, "Verification"): each check's name, the pattern of the changed files that call for it, its command, and why. Data, not code: tools/quick.mjs reads it, and the workflow policy (.github/scripts/policy/) reads it as data and never runs it, so that no edit to it changes what the policy does. Each pattern is a regular expression over a path relative to the repository's root, with forward slashes.

checks.name: gates
checks.why: The repository's gates: English text, the dependency policy, the lock's crates.

checks.name: lint list, golden files and conformance
checks.why: What a change to the compiler or to its programs must keep: the lint's list of what it does not see, the golden files every conformance program writes, and each program's expected report.

checks.name: MIR mutation gate
checks.why: The gate's records name each mutant by the MIR it changes, so a change to MIR, to the lowering or to the gate can add, drop or rename a mutant, which only the gate's own tests see (PR 158: an operation made exact stopped verifying, and the gate's records named a mutant that no longer existed, which CI found and these checks had not run).

checks.name: demo mutation gate
checks.why: `mn test --mutate` runs the same gate on the corpus, through the command.

checks.name: program generator
checks.why: The program generator's own tests, one filter for each module of its directory: every construct of the grammar reached, every generated program well typed and replayable, the three paths agreeing on them, and the host's shapes. No other check runs them, so a change to the generator passed these checks and failed only on CI (compiler-fixes, 2026-11-22). The policy's check "tools/quick.mjs runs the program generator's own tests for a change to it" holds a filter here for each module of the directory.

checks.name: workflow policy
checks.why: The workflow policy reads files across the whole tree, not the gates alone: every module a job that holds a secret runs, the compiler's sources for its ignored tests, the corpus, the spec and the docs. So any change can fail it, and every change calls for it (PR 161: a change to the benchmark's harness alone failed it in CI, where this map had not run it). The policy's check "tools/quick.mjs runs this policy before a push for a change to any file" holds this.

checks.name: local limits
checks.why: The local limits proved on this machine: a process past its memory dies alone, a command past its time ends with its children, a third build waits for a slot, a killed holder frees its slot, and -MenteOnly leaves other projects untouched. They run on Windows alone, so CI does not run them. The policy's check "the quick checks run every command in one of the machine's build slots, under the local limits" holds this.

checks.name: quick's own report
checks.why: tools/quick.mjs says, at the end of a listing and of a run, whether its checks read HEAD's tree, before them and after, or a tree that differs from it or changed while they ran, and writes the tree a passing run read (#174's merge c94b58e left two resolved files unstaged, and these checks passed on the working tree). Its test runs the real script in a repository it makes, with shims for the checks' commands, so it depends on local-limits.mjs and store-apps.mjs too. CI runs it in the Documentation job.

checks.name: the push guard
checks.why: git's pre-push hook of this repository (tools/git-hooks/pre-push, tools/push.mjs), which refuses a push of a commit whose tree tools/quick.mjs has not passed, run by real pushes to a bare remote its test makes, and the narrow rule of .claude/settings.json against bypassing it. It reads commands with raw-build.mjs and the record's name from local-limits.mjs. CI runs it in the Documentation job.
